# Code of Conduct

## The standard

Be respectful and direct. Critique work, never people. Assume competence and good faith in others,
and extend the benefit of the doubt you would want extended to you.

Contributors here come from different countries, languages, backgrounds, and levels of experience.
English is a second language for many, including the maintainer. Judge the substance of what someone
wrote, not the fluency of it.

## Expected

- Disagree about technical matters plainly, with reasons and evidence.
- Accept a decision you argued against, once it is made and recorded.
- Say "I do not know" and "I was wrong" without ceremony. Both are ordinary here.
- Ask before assuming a mistake was carelessness.

## Not accepted

- Personal attacks, insults, or demeaning comments about a person or a group.
- Harassment of any kind, in issues, pull requests, or private contact arising from this project.
- Discriminatory language or conduct on any basis.
- Publishing someone's private information without their explicit permission.
- Sustained disruption: repeatedly reopening settled decisions, or arguing in bad faith.

## Scope

This applies in every space this project occupies — issues, pull requests, discussions, commit
messages, and code review — and to any private contact that arises from participating here.

## Enforcement

Report a concern privately to the maintainer through GitHub. Reports are handled discreetly; the
reporter's identity is not shared without their consent.

Responses are proportionate: a private word first, then a warning, then removal of the ability to
participate. A first-time misstep handled gracefully ends there. Repeated or deliberate conduct does
not.

The maintainer applies this document to everyone, including themselves.
